comments.note: test_activeSortColumn_hasIndicator only exercises SORT_ASC. A companion test for SORT_DESC active column would improve direction-indicator coverage, though the existing assertion (▲ or ▼) is flexible enough to be renderer-agnostic.

No test verifies a grid with multiple sortable columns: only the active column should show the sort indicator while inactive sortable columns show plain sort links. This is a nice-to-have scenario for future expansion.

summary: Reviewed tests/Sorting/RendererSortHeaderTest.php against all four review dimensions.
No blocking issues found. Code is clean, correct, and fully consistent with project conventions.
File opens with declare(strict_types=1). Namespace AppUtils\Tests\Sorting is correct.
setUp/tearDown pattern (save/restore $_GET and $_SERVER['REQUEST_URI'] with null guard) is byte-for-byte consistent with ColumnSortingTest.php — test isolation is sound.
Five test methods cover the required acceptance criteria: non-sortable/sortable/active-sort for base renderer, non-sortable/sortable for Bootstrap5.
test_bootstrap5_sortableColumn_hasBootstrapClasses correctly validates the 5 Bootstrap5-specific CSS classes injected by the createSortAnchor() override in Bootstrap5Renderer.
One non-blocking imprecision noted in test_activeSortColumn_hasIndicator (see comments). All pre-existing non-blocking gaps (SORT_DESC, multi-column) acknowledged and do not block.

comments.note: test_activeSortColumn_hasIndicator sets DataGridInterface::SORT_ASC explicitly, so the expected indicator is always ▲. Using assertTrue(str_contains($html,'▲') || str_contains($html,'▼')) is overly permissive — it would pass even if ▼ were rendered by mistake. Prefer assertStringContainsString('▲', $html) for precision. Non-blocking: the current codebase cannot produce a false positive here.

No SORT_DESC active-sort test exists. The SORT_ASC path exercises the ternary in BaseGridRenderer::createSortAnchor() but the SORT_DESC branch (returning ▼) is untested. A companion test_activeSortColumn_descHasDownIndicator would complete direction-coverage symmetry. Low priority, do not block.

No multi-column indicator test: a grid with two sortable columns where only the active column shows a direction indicator and the other shows a plain link. Nice-to-have for future expansion, already flagged by QA. Do not block.
No other observations — code is clean, well-structured, and follows all project conventions. Assertion verbs are idiomatic. Bootstrap5-specific class coverage is complete and precise.
